title: Action plan cards grooming notes and wireframe sketch
content:
Status: exploratory grooming + quick wire sketches (v0.3)
Author: Samantha Reyes (prod-optimize)
Contributors: Arjun Patel (eng-serving-runtime), Mina Korhonen (designer), Diego Alvarez (analytics)

Objective:
- Define a minimal, high-value UX for surfaced optimization recommendations (batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles) that engineers can preview, simulate, and apply with safe rollouts.
- Focus on clarity of impact (latency, cost, quality) and low-risk application flows (dry-run, canary, revert).

Goals & success metrics for MVP:
- Time-to-apply for a single recommendation < 3 minutes (measured via telemetry).
- Acceptance rate (applied/accepted suggestions) > 20% in first 6 weeks for internal pilot teams.
- No regression incidents caused by auto-applied quantization > 0 in pilot window.

Personas:
- ML platform engineer: wants precise control and clear rollback; cares about throughput and tail latency.
- Product engineer: wants simple, low-risk knobs with observable delta in cost and response quality.
- SRE: needs audit trail, who-applied, and safety guardrails for production models.

Core concept: "Action cards"
- Each recommendation surfaces as a card in the Optimize > Recommendations panel.
- Card summary line shows: recommendation type, expected delta (cost/latency), confidence score, and an action menu.
- Expand to view: before/after preview, short rationale, measured evidence (simulated or historical), and quick apply controls.

Card anatomy (compact and expanded):
- Compact row: [ICON] Title (e.g., "Enable prefix KV caching for /api/chat")  •  Expected: -18% p50 latency  •  +0.4% cost  •  Confidence: 78%  •  [Apply] [Preview]

- Expanded view fields:
  * Rationale: short bullet, e.g., "Large number of repeated prefixes, high cache hit potential"
  * Evidence: 30-day sample: baseline p50 87ms -> simulated p50 71ms; tokens saved: ~120k/day
  * Suggested parameters: batch_size: 32 -> 64; cache_policy: prefix (TTL 600s); quant_profile: q4f16 (recommended)
  * Risk notes: "Quantization may slightly change logits; suggested to run quality check set 1"
  * Controls: [Dry-run simulate] [Apply (canary)] [Add to collection] [Dismiss]

Quick wireframe (ASCII sketch)
--------------------------------------------------
| Recommendations (Optimize)                        |
|  Filter: model, route, priority [v]  Sort: impact |
|-------------------------------------------------|
| [Card] Title  -18% latency  78% conf   [Apply]   |
| > Expand to show chart + params  [Preview]       |
|-------------------------------------------------|
| [Card] Title  -9% cost  63% conf    [Apply]     |
| ...                                            |
--------------------------------------------------

Preview / Dry-run mode:
- Goal: let users simulate expected performance/cost impact without changing live routing.
- Implementation hint: run a short forward simulation against sampled traces (1h sample) on staging model variant. Show side-by-side token-by-token delta and a simple flag if "quality checks" fail.
- UI: toggles for sample window, which metric to prioritize (latency/cost/quality), and option to persist simulation config for later.

Apply flow variants:
1) Single apply -> open modal: select target environment (staging/production/dedicated pool), choose rollout: instant | gradual (x% traffic) | schedule (time), confirm reviewers, run quick safety checks.
2) Bulk apply -> multi-select cards -> batch modal with aggregated expected delta and ability to create a rollout plan for all picks.
3) Auto-apply rules (future): allow platform to auto-surface and auto-apply low-risk suggestions under policy (requires QA flag and enterprise approval).

Safety & telemetry requirements:
- Every apply must produce an audit event: actor, time, config diff, target routes, pre-apply baseline snapshot.
- Pre-apply quality check: run configured small eval prompt set; fail means block unless override by manager.
- Post-apply regression monitoring: auto-create alert if p95 latency increases > X% or quality score drops > Y%.

Backlog grooming (stories and rough estimates)
- EPIC: Action cards v0 (6 sprints)
  * Story 1 (3): UX: compact + expanded card templates, filter/sort, basic states (applied, dismissed)
  * Story 2 (5): Backend: recommendations API endpoint with scoring + evidence payload (enable pagination and grouping by route)
  * Story 3 (5): Simulator: dry-run engine prototype (1h sample runner) + preview API
  * Story 4 (3): Apply modal + rollout options (canary strategy) + audit logging
  * Story 5 (3): Acceptance tests: quality-check harness + blocking logic for quantization recommendations
  * Story 6 (2): Analytics: event schema for applied/dismissed/previewed; dashboard prototype
  * Bonus (3): Bulk-apply / collection work for power users

Priorities (initial pilot): Story 1, Story 2, Story 3 -> minimum shippable set to let a small customer pilot recommendations in staging.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Cards render with evidence and parameters for >80% of rule-generated recs in sample dataset.
- Dry-run returns simulated cost/latency deltas in <60s for 1h sample on our staging cluster.
- Apply modal records audit event and triggers canary rollout according to chosen percent.
- Post-apply monitors register and link to the change.

Open questions / decisions for PM + Eng:
- Quality gating threshold: what is acceptable default (1% absolute quality delta? 3% relative?)
- Simulator sample size: default to 1h trace or configurable? Implications on runtime and cost.
- Quantization labeling: do we surface internal terms (q4f16) or friendly names ("balanced-4b")?
- Permissions: which roles can auto-apply suggestions vs only propose? Do we need separate approvals for quantization?

Notes for design handoff:
- Visual affordance: use color accents for expected positive impact (green/blue) and caution (amber) for potential quality risk.
- Microcopy: every card must have a 1-line "why this matters" plus a one-sentence "what changes" before the user hits Apply.
- Charts: show p50/p95 and token savings in small inline sparkline. Clicking opens full metrics page.

Telemetry & analytics spec (short):
- Events: recommendation_view, recommendation_preview, recommendation_apply_started, recommendation_apply_completed, recommendation_dismissed, recommendation_collect_added
- Attributes: rec_id, rec_type, model, route, expected_delta_latency_pct, expected_delta_cost_pct, confidence, actor_id, env_target, rollout_type
- Dashboard: adoption funnel (view->preview->apply), mean impact per rec type, failure rate by rec type

Prototype links + artifacts:
- Figma proto: https://figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/optimize-action-cards-proto (annotated frames: compact, expanded, modal, dry-run)
- Simulation POC (internal): https://internal.redwood.ai/sim/opt-recs-proto
- Jira epic: PROD-OPT-842 (action-cards)

Next steps (this week):
- PM: finalize gating thresholds and list of pilot routes (Samantha).
- Eng: quick spike for dry-run simulator (Arjun) — 2 day spike to validate 1h sample runtime.
- Designer: polish compact card and microcopy (Mina) and upload updated frames by EOD Thursday.
- Analytics: event schema proposal and pipeline cost estimate (Diego).

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: quantization introduces subtle quality changes -> Mitigation: require quality-check pass and explicit manager approval for quantization applies in production.
- Risk: simulator runtime costs -> Mitigation: cap sample size in UI and provide cost estimate before running.

Notes to reviewer:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and sketchy; aim is to converge on the apply flow and safety checks before investing in polished visuals. Please comment directly in the Figma frames for the compact/expanded variations and add +1 in Jira PROD-OPT-842 if your team wants to be in pilot.

Changelog:
- v0.1 (2025-01-22) initial scribbles
- v0.2 (2025-01-30) added dry-run concept and telemetry list
- v0.3 (2025-02-04) grooming notes and story point estimates (this doc)

-- end --
